title: Isaac Newton lost a fortune in a stock bubble
caption:
In 1720, everyone in London wanted shares of the South Sea Company.
Isaac Newton bought in, sold for a profit, then watched the price keep climbing.
Then the bubble burst. Newton reportedly lost around twenty thousand pounds.
He is said to have written: I can calculate the motions of the heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people.
comment: Have you ever bought because everyone else was? 👇
sources: Andrew Odlyzko, 'Newton's financial misadventures in the South Sea Bubble' (Royal Society, 2019)
